raw_text:
- The study's objective is to understand why sites with identical nominal work processes experience different completion times.
- The scope includes analyzing measurable factors contributing to completion-time differences in work processes.

Assumptions
- Site work processes can be theoretically modeled and observed.
- The study focuses on measurable factors affecting completion time.

Research design
- The study uses the software-testing methodological approach to gather and analyze data.
- A comparative case study will be conducted with multiple cases of sites using different nominal work processes.

Data or evidence needed
- Completion-time data for each site with a nominal work process.
- System descriptions and documentation for each site.

Measurement
- Completion times will be measured and coded for analysis.
- Process measures will be recorded for each site, such as cycle time and task durations.

Analysis
- A regression analysis will be conducted to determine the relationships between process measures and completion times.
- Factor analysis will be used to identify common factors across sites.

Decision / stopping rule
- The decision rule is to stop when no new patterns or insights emerge after regression and factor analyses.

Limitations
- Limited to sites with available data and those willing to participate.
- Potential for self-selection bias among participating sites.
